question: Do the three retained patterns exclude ordinary left attachment, or only extra exhaustive one-to-one pairing?
result: They do not exclude ordinary left attachment. A left-extensible expression plus unmodified heads supplies token-conserving counterparses.
formal_rules: For this counterexample only, H labels chol tokens and M labels daiin tokens; these are NOT established manuscript lexical categories.
E -> H | E M; a sequence may contain more than one E.
H may occur without M; M may extend an already modified expression. Both freedoms are declared, not facts inferred about native words.
stronger_model_that_fails: Every token in each independently closed three-token window must belong to exactly one disjoint immediate H-M pair. This is stronger than either a direction or a modifier hypothesis. The window is not independently a native closed unit.
right_attachment_limit: H M H can be H [M H]. H M M and H H M need an explicitly available later head if every M is a right modifier. Absence of that head within a selected window alone does not exclude right attachment globally, and an unseen head must not be invented as observed.
global_countercases: 1047 remains binding: exact daiin left-host requirement within recorded paragraphs has0ZL but2ITcontradictions driven by paragraph flags; right-host requirement25/26. RF lacks paragraph flags. Local countergrammar is not a rescue of the failed universal contracts.
difference_from1201: 1201 proves that some multiple parses preserve one stipulated message. Here only existence of local bracketings is shown; no message or semantic equality is defined.
decision: Do not infer mandatory complex state, several hidden referents, corruption or a universal two-word unit from these three patterns. No recursive-native-syntax or modifier meaning selected. New work requires an independently supported binding domain or role consequence, after prior review; no new count/simulator.
independent_review: Authorized bounded producer separately supplied the same left counterparses and right-domain caveat; no new data opened.
